messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The cracks are showing—small things, but they’re adding up. The regime’s still standing, but it’s leaning harder on the walls than it lets on. Keep your eyes open, but don’t rush—this could tip either way if the wrong person stumbles."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm warning, more like the quiet before something shifts. The old guard is still standing, but the cracks are showing in the way they move, not just what they say. Keep your ears open, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time for bold steps, just quiet ones."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s chipping in places—small cracks, but they’re there. People are starting to whisper ‘maybe’ instead of ‘never,’ but no one’s shouting yet. Keep your eyes open, but don’t bet the house just because the foundation’s creaking."*"
Sender 4: "*"Things feel like they’re shifting—less like a storm coming and more like the ground is softening underfoot. People are talking more openly, but no one’s sure if that’s a sign of weakness or just the regime tightening its grip before the next move. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels like the moment before a storm—no one’s sure if it’ll break or pass, but everyone’s holding their breath. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like a house of cards: one wrong move, and the whole thing could wobble. Let’s stay sharp, but quiet—no need to rush anything."*"
Sender 6: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual signs are all there: contracts moving, money flowing, even the streets staying quiet when they could’ve gotten loud. But don’t mistake quiet for weak. The inner circle’s tightening, not cracking, and the watchers are sharper than ever. Still, a few of us are tucking things away just in case—no need to rush, but no harm in being ready."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—like something’s shifting, but slowly, like the tide pulling back before a storm. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 8: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are showing—more in the whispers than the headlines. The usual optimists and pessimists are suddenly on the same page, and that’s what worries me. Let’s keep our circles tight and our ears open."*"
Sender 9: "*"The machine is still running, but the gears are grinding louder than usual—pay delays, empty promises, and even the usual watchdogs seem distracted. The market women are talking freely now, and the embassies are suddenly moving slower. Nothing’s breaking yet, but the cracks are showing. Stay sharp, but don’t step where you can’t see the ground."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different this month—less like the usual grumbling and more like people are starting to move in the same direction, even if just in whispers. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore, and the way they’re reacting tells me they know it too. Stay sharp, and let’s keep this quiet."*"
Sender 11: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a stack of plates someone’s trying not to drop. The regime’s still in charge, but the cracks are showing, and the younger ones aren’t waiting to see if they’ll hold. Let’s stay sharp, but quiet—this could tip either way, and we don’t want to be the ones who push it."*"
Sender 12: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—small shifts in the ranks, the usual noise getting louder in private, and the regime’s grip tightening just enough to make you wonder what they’re bracing for. Keep your eyes open, but no sudden moves—this isn’t the time to test the edges."*"
Sender 13: "*"Things are holding for now, but the cracks are showing in ways that worry me—like how the old guard is suddenly sticking together like glue, or how even the hardliners in the security forces are quietly stepping back from the front lines. The money’s still flowing, but only if you take it in dollars now, and the censors are scrambling to keep up instead of staying ahead. It’s not collapse yet, but it’s not stability either—more like a dam with too many leaks, and no one’s sure which one will break first."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different—like the regime’s holding its breath, not just tightening its grip. The cracks are there, but no one’s sure if they’ll split open or just get papered over. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could be the calm before the storm or just another false alarm."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s saying it out loud. The usual signs are there, but quieter, like people are holding their breath. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could be the calm before something, and we don’t know which way it’ll break."*"
Sender 16: "*"Things feel quieter, but not steady—like the calm before something, not the calm after. The elites are hedging, the security forces are dragging their feet, and the money’s still moving, just slower. People aren’t even whispering about change anymore, just waiting to see what happens next. That might be the most worrying part."*"
Sender 17: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now, but it’s all too quiet—like everyone’s holding their breath. The regime’s still in charge, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, stay safe, and let’s keep our ears to the ground."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for something to shift. The usual cracks are showing, but nothing’s breaking yet. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for safety."*"
Sender 19: "*"Things are shifting, but no one’s sure which way—even the people who should know. The regime’s still standing, but it feels like a house of cards: one strong breeze, and it could go either way. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’re not there. And for now, keep your heads down."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things feel like they’re holding together, but it’s the kind of holding that makes you nervous—like a dam with too many cracks you can’t see. The inner circle’s grip is tighter, but the cracks are showing in the little things: orders get dragged out, the propaganda’s running on autopilot, and even the embassies are quietly packing their bags. No one’s moving yet, but the air’s different—like everyone’s waiting for the first real push, one way or the other."*"
Sender 21: "*"Things are holding for now, but it feels like we’re all just waiting for the next gust of wind—no one’s sure which way it’ll blow. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding louder than ever, and the people who usually know these things? Even they’re just guessing at this point."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially when the same people keep whispering the same warnings without ever meeting. The regime’s still in control, but it’s starting to feel like they’re rearranging the deck chairs while the ship tilts. Stay sharp, and let’s keep our circles tight."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—small signs, but not enough to call it a storm yet. The old guard is tightening its grip, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t move until we’re sure which way the wind is blowing."*"
Sender 24: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are starting to show—just enough to notice if you’re looking. The air’s different, like everyone’s waiting for something, but no one’s sure what yet. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves."*"
Sender 25: "*"Things feel like they’re holding together for now, but the cracks are showing—even the regime’s own people are hesitating, and the mood on the street is more ‘waiting to see’ than ‘ready to act.’ We’re not there yet, but the air is different. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could go either way."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
